description: The line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) across eight different sports categories — cf, bb, WNBA, ESPN, NHL, FIFA, Estadio, and athletics — under a clean-label poisoning attack scenario with a poison rate of 10% (2.5% of total data), as described in the paper “Efficient Trigger Word Insertion.” The x-axis lists the sports categories as categorical labels, while the y-axis represents ASR on a linear scale ranging from 0.5 to 0.95, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. Three distinct lines are plotted: a green line with circle markers labeled “start,” an orange line with cross markers labeled “end,” and a purple line with circle markers also labeled “end” in the legend (though visually it appears to represent a separate trajectory). The green “start” line begins at approximately 0.77 for “cf,” drops sharply to 0.49 at “bb,” rises to 0.90 at “WNBA,” dips to 0.82 at “ESPN,” climbs to 0.84 at “NHL,” peaks at 0.93 at “Estadio,” and ends at 0.93 for “athletics.” The orange “end” line starts at 0.66 for “cf,” falls to 0.51 at “bb,” surges to 0.88 at “WNBA,” drops to 0.72 at “ESPN,” rises to 0.77 at “NHL,” peaks at 0.93 at “Estadio,” and declines to 0.87 at “athletics.” The purple “end” line begins at 0.76 for “cf,” drops to 0.57 at “bb,” jumps to 0.88 at “WNBA,” dips to 0.75 at “ESPN,” rises to 0.89 at “NHL,” falls to 0.81 at “FIFA,” peaks at 0.97 at “Estadio,” and ends at 0.83 for “athletics.” The plot visually compares the evolution of ASR from initial to final states across domains, with notable variability and peaks around “Estadio.”
